digest.component_or_area: LLM signed verdict assembly and persistence across plan-review, completion, and code-review gates
propositions: Signed verdicts currently record only a model string and cannot distinguish between verdicts produced by different providers or tiers (first-class vs best-effort), creating ambiguity when verdicts are persisted behind opaque gateways.

A new additive `provider_provenance` object must be stamped alongside the existing model field, carrying provider, model, endpoint_host, tier, and effective capabilities, while preserving backward compatibility for readers that encounter payloads without it.

The provenance record must be assembled once in runner.py from primitives already held in scope, reusing the single-computed capabilities record to avoid divergence from the actual record that drove the run.
Endpoint host extraction must use `urlparse(base_url).hostname` rather than `.netloc` to ensure credentials embedded in base_url never appear in the persisted payload.

The provider_provenance field must be threaded through all three sidecar build_payload functions (plan-review, completion, code-review) and into the signed manifest so that consumers can verify the tier of a verdict.
Backward compatibility is ensured by making provider_provenance optional; legacy payloads without the key must still load, verify, and be handled gracefully by downstream consumers.
